dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Welcome to WKU Radio. Today I'm speaking with Zhibek Akhmetova, captain of the WKU women's volleyball team. Zhibek, how long have you been playing volleyball?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've been playing since I was nine years old. So — almost fifteen years.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: That's incredible. What has been the highlight of your career so far?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Winning the regional championship in 2022 was the most important moment. We've worked so hard for that and it finally happened.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Yes — I've represented Kazakhstan in two under-23 tournaments. One in Bishkek, one in Tashkent. It was a completely different level.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: What has been the hardest moment in your career?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Injuring my shoulder twice. The second time was worse. I was out for six months. I thought about stopping completely.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: No. I've never been someone who gives up easily. I came back and I was stronger.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Beyond volleyball, what have you achieved academically at WKU?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've maintained a GPA above 3.8 throughout my degree. I've also written two research papers — one of them has been accepted for publication.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Impressive. What has been the most surprising thing you've discovered about yourself at university?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That I'm genuinely interested in sports science. I've started reading research papers on training methodology. I've realised that what I want isn't just to play — I want to understand sport at a deeper level.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: What are your plans after graduation?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've already applied for a master's in sports science in Almaty. And I'm going to try one more time for the national championship this spring.

questions.text: "I've been playing since I was nine." — Why use PP here?
opts: It started in the past and continues now
questions.correct: It started in the past and continues now
questions.hint: "have been playing" = Present Perfect Continuous — started past, still continuing NOW. "since" confirms it.

questions.text: "One of them ___ (accept/passive) for publication." Use Present Perfect.
questions.hint: Present Perfect passive: "has been + past participle". "One has been ACCEPTED." ✅

questions.text: "I was out for six months." — Why Past Simple here?
opts: It happened in the past and is completed
questions.correct: It happened in the past and is completed
questions.hint: The injury period is OVER and completed → Past Simple. If it still continued, she'd use PP.

questions.text: "We've worked so hard for that and it finally happened." — why PP then PS?
opts: PP = process (ongoing to past); PS = specific completed event
questions.correct: PP = process (ongoing to past); PS = specific completed event
questions.hint: "We've worked" = PP (the effort over time). "It finally happened" = PS (the specific moment it occurred).

questions.text: "What has been the highlight so far?" — "so far" means:
opts: Up to this point in time
questions.correct: Up to this point in time
questions.hint: "so far" = from the beginning until now. Often used with PP: "What have you achieved so far?"

questions.text: "She ___ (never / give up) easily." Use Present Perfect.
questions.hint: "give up → given up" (irregular). "She's never given up easily." ✅

questions.text: "I've already applied." — "already" goes where in a PP sentence?
opts: After the subject, before the past participle
questions.correct: After the subject, before the past participle
questions.hint: "I've ALREADY applied." = Subject + have/has + ALREADY + past participle. ✅

questions.text: "I've maintained a GPA of 3.8 throughout my degree." This means:
questions.hint: "throughout my degree" = for the entire duration, consistently. PP shows ongoing result.
